failure_reason: wait_sim_terminal.py ran under the system Python 3.12 instead of the runtime virtualenv 3.10, so rclpy's C extension was absent (ModuleNotFoundError: rclpy._rclpy_pybind11) and every attempt died about fifteen seconds after launch
root_cause: the episode script invoked bare 'python', resolving the interpreter from PATH. Identity 180 succeeded because it was launched from a script that activated the virtualenv; the detached batch invokes the virtualenv interpreter directly without activating, so PATH still pointed at the system Python
resolution: the episode script now resolves the interpreter explicitly (LIVIFUSER_PYTHON, then the runtime virtualenv, then python3) and asserts it can import rclpy immediately after both ROS setups are sourced, so a wrong interpreter fails in one second rather than after a launch
changed: scripts/run_live_sim_development_episode.sh: explicit interpreter resolution and an rclpy assertion
